main_body: Tall brick townhouse with a slate mansard roof, a dormer and a chimney on top, three storeys of windows, a balcony and a green door
top_band: Light slate-grey roof top, rows 17-22 (L 95-122), with a lighter edge row 23, then a dark eave row 24 and the darker slate slope below
evidence: Column x=24 reads: outline row 16, light roof-top band rows 17-22, edge line row 23 (L122), dark eave row 24 (L53), then the slate slope and the brick facade. The roof top is a 6-row horizontal band clearly separate from the front, which has a step of more than 25 L, an edge line and an eave shadow. The facade is a flat front view, but windows with sills and frames, a balcony and a door canopy give it depth, and the roof surface reads as a top. Weak but acceptable 3/4 for a building.

style.evidence: The brick, slate and stone trim each carry several tones, with brick mortar texture and lit windows. The measured facts count against it: 90% of dark edge pixels are neutral (references 7-9%), and the dark rows (#14181f, #1d1722) are near-colourless outlines, which gives the sticker look. It has only 49 distinct colours against 185 and 66 for the references. Colours per tile (14) are within the reference range, and flat-fill coverage is a low 2%. The outline craft is the weakness against the Beodeul standard, so it fails.
